Ward 5 has public parks and playgrounds close to almost every home. But how many people share them? This is amenities against population, measured the same way for every ward in Calgary.

First, distance. Ninety-nine percent of homes in Ward 5 are within four hundred metres of a public park, about the same as Calgary as a whole. And seventy-nine percent are within four hundred metres of a playground, more than Calgary's seventy-one percent.

Now, crowding. Take the park space within reach of each home, and share it among everyone who can reach it. Ward 5 has about two point nine hectares of park for every thousand residents. Calgary has five point nine. That is about half, and the second lowest of the fourteen wards.
Playgrounds tell the same story. Within four hundred metres, Ward 5 has about two playgrounds for every thousand children under fifteen, against four across Calgary. That is the lowest of any ward.

Why? Homes in Ward 5 are fuller. The 2021 Census counted three point six people per household, against two point six in Calgary, and three in ten residents were under twenty. The same parks are shared by more people, and more children.

Community by community, against Calgary's level of one. Redstone, Saddle Ridge, Skyview Ranch and Taradale have well under half of Calgary's park space per person. For playgrounds, Cityscape, Falconridge and Skyview Ranch are the most crowded.

How it is measured: every park's area is shared among the residents within four hundred metres of its edge, and every playground among the children nearby. Each home then adds up its shares. A score of one means the same as Calgary. Every ward and community is measured the same way on the Growth versus amenities screen.
Calgary Data Desk, by Hassan Ali. Near is not the same as enough.
